Description: Tusla hereby invites suitably qualified and experienced Service Providers to submit tenders for the provision of Children’s Residential Services to complement existing community based residential services operated by/on behalf of Tusla. Please note that this tender was previously published on 09/03/2026 under the following eTenders Resource ID: 7641990 and OJEU Reference Number 2026- 162039 with the following title; Bespoke Panel Arrangement for the Provision of Children’s Residential Services to Complement Existing Community Based Residential Services Operated by/on Behalf of Tusla Following that competition a bespoke panel has been established and contracts have been awarded to successful tenderers. The purpose of this Contract Notice is to fulfil the obligations of the original bespoke panel competition by reopening the competition to interested parties as set out in Section 1.13 of the original Invitation to Tender. In that context, Service Providers that believe that they have the requisite capacity, suitability qualified staff, experience and expertise within their organisation to deliver the services required as outlined in the tender documentation, are invited to submit tenders for the provision of Children’s Residential Services to complement existing community based residential services operated by / on behalf of Tusla. Tusla now invites organisations to tender to join a Bespoke Panel Arrangement to provide high quality Children’s Residential Services. Requirements which arise under the Arrangement will be procured using spot purchasing. The Rates for services are set in the tender documents and interested parties applying to participate on the panel will be required to sign a declaration within the Tender Response Document. By signing the declaration, Applicants declaration confirms their agreement to these rates. It is envisaged that all the required services of this tender will be funded and managed by Tusla. This tender process is being conducted under Annex XIV of Procurement directives 2014/24/EU. The goal is the development of a reliable, turn-key calibration system, which covers the optical and NIR spectral range (0.37-1.8 µm) offered by ESO’s instruments with (tens of) thousands of unresolved spectral lines. The wavelengths of the individual calibration lines should be known from first principles to an accuracy equal or better than 1cm/s. The immediate objectives of the project are to determine the most promising technology and technical implementation of such a calibration system, based on one or two design studies and to increase the technical readiness through prototyping where necessary. The long-term goal is the development, production and delivery of the system. The contract covering this latter phase may be placed without further competition. According to the current plan, the design studies should start in Q4 2022. The initial design studies should take approx. 12 months, starting right after the contract award. The goal is to kick-off the development/production contract about one year after concluding the study contracts. ESO intends to release a RFI in Q1/Q2 2022. Scheduled/Status:
